dimensions.label: Cheapest way onto your own custom domain
dimensions.a: $25/mo (Basic) — a custom domain, but no CMS or blog
dimensions.b: $25/mo (Basic) — same price, and it already includes a blog, store and invoicing

dimensions.label: What happens to the bill as traffic grows
dimensions.a: Premium includes only 50 GB bandwidth a month; more traffic means a metered add-on
dimensions.b: Unlimited bandwidth on every current plan; traffic growth alone never raises the bill

dimensions.label: Cost of adding team members past the owner
dimensions.a: $19/mo for every extra Limited seat, on any Workspace, with no headcount limit
dimensions.b: Basic allows 2 people total; Core and up remove the cap for $39/mo, with no per-seat fee

dimensions.label: CMS and content scale at the matching plan price
dimensions.b: Core, $39/mo: no cap on blog posts; store products capped at 10,000 sitewide

dimensions.label: Cheapest path to a 0% product transaction fee
dimensions.a: Needs Ecommerce Plus at $84/mo; the entry Ecommerce Standard plan ($42/mo) charges 2%
dimensions.b: Needs only Core at $39/mo; the entry Basic plan ($25/mo) charges 2%

dimensions.label: Selling digital products, courses or memberships
dimensions.a: No published fee tier for digital products or memberships
dimensions.b: Built in, stepping from 7% on Basic to 0% on Advanced, $139/mo

dimensions.label: Trying it before you commit
dimensions.a: A free Starter plan with no time limit, but no custom domain
dimensions.b: A 14-day free trial of a real paid plan, but it can't take real payments

dimensions.label: Refund window if you change your mind
dimensions.a: Any new Site or Workspace purchase, monthly or annual, within 14 days
dimensions.b: Only a new annual plan's first payment, within 14 days; monthly plans aren't refundable

dimensions.label: Design freedom vs. a guided editor
dimensions.a: Full visual control over layout and custom code; a real learning curve
dimensions.b: Guided sections and blocks; faster to start, less layout freedom

dimensions.label: AI credits included each month
dimensions.a: 200-400 credits a month across Workspace plans, reset monthly, no rollover
dimensions.b: Basic gets 10 one-time credits only; Core and up add 20-120 renewing credits a month

verdicts.why: Webflow's Agency Workspace bundles unlimited staging sites and free client seats for exactly this job, while Squarespace bills every client site as its own separate account.
Squarespace prices digital-content sales on a published, falling fee scale, which fits selling a course better than Webflow's ecommerce plans, built around a shipped product catalog.

A real product catalog outgrows both: Webflow's ecommerce plans cap out at 15,000 items with an entry-tier fee, and Squarespace's store is a feature bundled into a site plan, not a dedicated back office.
Squarespace gets a booking-and-invoicing-ready site live without anyone on staff who can design from scratch, which suits a busy local-service owner better than Webflow's visual canvas.
A freelancer building sites for other people gets Webflow's Freelancer Workspace, built around staging sites and a free client seat per project, with no Squarespace equivalent.
A startup's marketing site benefits from Webflow's custom code and Webflow Cloud app hosting, neither of which has an equivalent in Squarespace's page-and-block editor.
